findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring indices
findings.body: The check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted: it rejects tokens whose grant shortcut matches the expected one. The substring indices are also wrong. The encoded prefix is 6 chars (session type, token type, grant type), so the grant shortcut sits at indices 4..6, not 3..5. As written the matcher rejects correct IDs and accepts almost any wrong one, so the event assertions are broken. It should be `!substring(4, 6).equals(expected)`.

findings.title: Null check on wrong variable for rawTokenId
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks grantType a second time, so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId is accepted and later encoded as the literal string "null".

findings.title: Lightweight-token detection depends on session context client, not the token's client
findings.body: `getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)` reads `session.getContext().getClient()`. That may be null, or a different client from the one the token is created for, for example during token exchange or when the context client is not set. This can cause an NPE, or an incorrect token type to be encoded.

findings.title: encodeTokenId throws for tokens created without a grant type attribute
findings.body: `initToken` is used by other paths that never set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, such as the implicit and hybrid flows and other callers of createClientAccessToken. In those cases the grant type defaults to "na". `encodeTokenId` then looks up the shortcut for "na", and while this works for the default provider, the generated ID carries an "na" grant type. For a custom grant whose factory is missing, the call throws IllegalStateException and the token request fails.

findings.title: Parsing a token ID throws on a non-matching prefix
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` splits at the first ':' and throws IllegalArgumentException if the prefix is not 6 chars. Third-party or older token IDs containing ':' would trigger exceptions in callers. Returning an UNKNOWN context would be safer.
